additions.node_text: שַׁבָּת הוּא שִׁי"ן בַּ"ת – שִׁי"ן תְּלַת גְּוָנִין דְּעֵינָא, בַּ"ת – בַּת עַיִן
additions.reason: The Torah deconstructs the word שַׁבָּת into its letters שִׁי"ן (= three colors of the eye) and בַּ"ת (= pupil of the eye). This is explicit bechina language equating שַׁבָּת with the eye's capacity to see. In this Torah, Shabbat enables seeing one's own שִׁפְלוּת — so שַׁבָּת as 'שִׁי"ן בַּ"ת' (= the faculty of true seeing) is a bechina of Shabbat in the same package as the rest of the שַׁבָּת cluster.
additions.source_quote: כִּי שַׁבָּ"ת הוּא שִׁי"ן בַּ"ת, שִׁי"ן – תְּלַת גְּוָנִין דְּעֵינָא, בַּ"ת – בַּת עַיִן, וְעַל כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת יָכוֹל לִרְאוֹת שִׁפְלוּתוֹ

additions.node_text: יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִדָּה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה
additions.reason: The Torah explicitly states that every true Tzaddik has a dimension of Mashiach, and Mashiach is a bechina of Moshe (citing Zohar 'מָשִׁיחַ דָּא מֹשֶׁה'). Additionally, the complete-teshuvah state is called 'בְּחִינוֹת מֹשֶׁה מָשִׁיחַ'. This is a cluster of at minimum three concepts (צַדִּיק, מֹשֶׁה, מָשִׁיחַ) all sharing the same essential nature — the self-sacrificing leader who knows his own smallness and the greatness of Israel. These nodes do not appear in the dataset for Torah 79 at all. They belong to a new package (see torah_79_new_packages.json).
additions.source_quote: מִי שֶׁהוּא צַדִּיק בֶּאֱמֶת, יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִדָּה שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה

additions.reason: The Torah contains explicit bechina language for at least four related concepts: שִׁפְלוּת (humility), עֲנָוָה (lowliness), the verse 'שְׁבוּ אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו' (as an expression of humility), and אַיִן (nothingness — the state of the truly humble person). These concepts share the same essential nature: true self-nullification, which protects livelihood and prevents displacement. These nodes do not appear in the bechina dataset for Torah 79. They belong to a new package (see torah_79_new_packages.json).
